name: Georgette Chen
method: Muse Spark web search (2 calls) for leads; every fact below re-read from the cited page by the agent. corroborated = two or more independent sources.

facts.text: Born Zhang Liying in October 1906 in Zhejiang, China, the fourth daughter of the wealthy merchant Zhang Jingjiang.

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)
Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'

facts.text: She was the fourth of 12 children.

sources.label: Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)
Wikipedia: Georgette Chen

facts.text: Her father was an antiques dealer with businesses in Paris, New York and London, and a close friend and financier of Sun Yat-sen.

sources.label: Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)
Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'
Wikipedia: Georgette Chen

facts.text: At home her mother allowed the children to speak only Shanghainese, and her father took the family on his trips to China so they would not forget where they came from.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Georgette Chen

facts.text: Her favourite childhood haunts in Paris were the Tuileries and Parc Monceau; decades later she still delighted in remembering the merry-go-round and feeding her favourite swans.

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

facts.text: She spent many childhood years in St Enogat, a village near Dinard in Brittany, and said France was in a way her home.

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

facts.text: Her father hired a private art tutor, Victor Podgorsky, and father and daughter attended the lessons together.

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

facts.text: Her father wanted her to study Chinese painting; she insisted on oils, so she could paint everything around her, down to salted ducks and potatoes.
facts.quote: My father expected me to study Chinese painting, but I had a different idea.
facts.speaker: Georgette Chen (Radio Malaya interview transcript, 7 Sep 1953, quoted in BiblioAsia)

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

facts.text: She remembered her father impatiently listing the Chinese vegetables she could paint instead, wanting to know why she insisted on the foreign potato.
facts.quote: He wanted to know why I insisted on painting the foreign potato.
facts.speaker: Georgette Chen (Straits Times, 30 Aug 1959, quoted in BiblioAsia)

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

facts.text: A 1923 class photograph shows her seated at the end of the front row at the Horace Mann School in New York; she also studied at the Lycee Jules-Ferry in Paris and McTyeire School for Girls in Shanghai.

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'

facts.text: Formal art training began with a year at the Art Students League of New York (1926-27).

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)
Wikipedia: Georgette Chen

facts.text: Back in Paris she enrolled at the loosely run Academie Colarossi and Academie Biloul and roamed the city for subjects, relishing 'the freedom of painting whatever you like'.
facts.quote: the freedom of painting whatever you like
facts.speaker: Georgette Chen (oral history with Constance Sheares, 1988)

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)

facts.text: Her parents paid for her art education but never fully accepted that she would be a full-time artist, fearing she could not make a living.

sources.label: Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)
Wikipedia: Georgette Chen

facts.text: At 21 she met Eugene Chen in Paris, introduced by their friend Soong Ching Ling (Madame Sun Yat-sen).

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'
Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)

facts.text: Eugene was 52, a widower with two sons and two daughters; his wife had died of cancer two years before.

sources.label: Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'

facts.text: Despite a 30-year age gap and her father's initial disapproval, the two became 'the closest of companions'.
facts.speaker: Georgette Chen (recollections of Eugene Chen, n.d., quoted in BiblioAsia)

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'

facts.text: The Salon d'Automne in Paris accepted her work for the first time.

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)
Wikipedia: Georgette Chen

facts.text: She married Eugene Chen at the Chinese Consular Office in Paris, took his surname, and kept it for the rest of her life, even after remarrying.

sources.label: Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'
Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)

facts.text: Eugene loved art, music and French literature, was always ready to pose, and told her to leave sewing to tailors and take up her easel instead.
facts.quote: He always told me not to sew because there were many tailors who could do the work.
facts.speaker: Georgette Chen (oral history with Constance Sheares, 1988)

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

facts.text: Her diary records the small joys of married life: giving Eugene a haircut, walking out together to hunt for pineapples and avocados to paint.
facts.quote: Begin small canvas of E portrait. Poses so badly & talks all the time.
facts.speaker: Georgette Chen (diary, quoted in BiblioAsia)

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

facts.text: After Eugene became foreign minister of the Nationalist government in 1931, the couple moved from Paris to Shanghai; on the ship from Marseilles to Singapore they met Tunku Abdul Rahman, who later remembered her 'beautiful and charming' presence; they became lifelong friends. (Tunku also painted by her in Kuala Lumpur, June 1956, per a BiblioAsia photo caption.)
facts.speaker: Tunku Abdul Rahman (quoted in BiblioAsia)

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'
Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)

facts.text: She took her first driving lesson on 7 June 1935, passed her test on 29 June, and bought a second-hand Fiat to drive around France painting outdoors.

sources.label: Michelle Tay, 'The World of Georgette Chen Archive', National Gallery Singapore magazine (2020)

facts.text: In July and August 1935 she drove to Aix-en-Provence and painted beside 'Cezanne's atelier', 'Cezanne's rocks at Chateau Noir' and his millstone.

sources.label: Michelle Tay, 'The World of Georgette Chen Archive', National Gallery Singapore magazine (2020)

facts.text: She showed at the Palace of Painting and Sculpture at the Paris World Fair and at Les Femmes Artistes d'Europe at the Jeu de Paume.

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)

facts.text: After the Japanese took Hong Kong, she and Eugene were placed under house arrest and later moved to Shanghai, where they were held.

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'

facts.text: Eugene was repeatedly called to Japanese 'interviews'; fearing for her safety, he insisted on taking her everywhere he went.

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

facts.text: Eugene died in Shanghai in May 1944, still under house arrest, leaving her a widow at 38.

sources.label: Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)
Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Wikipedia: Georgette Chen

facts.text: She held a solo show of some 77 works in Shanghai, then left for New York to marry Ho Yung Chi, Eugene's former aide and an old friend.

sources.label: Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'
Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)

facts.text: The couple took teaching posts at Han Chiang High School in Penang, which she called 'a beautiful tropical island which I call my Tahiti'.
facts.quote: a beautiful tropical island which I call my Tahiti
facts.speaker: Georgette Chen (letter to Inez, 20 Mar 1966)

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Wikipedia: Georgette Chen

facts.text: A few months after arriving she wrote that the waterfront huts made her 'shout with excitement', and that the durian had enriched her life.
facts.quote: I have been introduced to the Durian fruit and consider that my life has been enriched by it!
facts.speaker: Georgette Chen (letter, 4 Jul 1951)

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Christie's, Georgette Chen, Still Life with Big Durian, lot essay (lot 6430010)

facts.text: The Penang years were soured by bitter arguments with Ho over money and her continued use of Eugene's surname; after a long, draining process they divorced in 1953, after six years.

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'

facts.text: In September 1953 she held her first solo exhibition in Singapore, at the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, and moved to Singapore the same year.

sources.label: Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'
Michelle Tay, 'The World of Georgette Chen Archive', National Gallery Singapore magazine (2020)
Wikipedia: Georgette Chen

facts.text: Settled in a rented house in Sennett Estate, she wrote to friends of a new, simpler life.
facts.quote: With my regained liberty, I now look forward to a simple, useful, and creative existence
facts.speaker: Georgette Chen (letter to friends, early 1954)

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

facts.text: She taught part-time at the Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts from 1954 to 1980, one of only two women teachers in its early years.

sources.label: Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'
Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)
Michelle Tay, 'The World of Georgette Chen Archive', National Gallery Singapore magazine (2020)

facts.text: She painted the Chen family of Penang (friends, not relatives) across several holiday visits; the father was only painted in later.
facts.quote: Every minute of your stay was enjoyable for me including the tantrums
facts.speaker: Georgette Chen (letter to the Chen family, 1955)

sources.label: Michelle Tay, 'The World of Georgette Chen Archive', National Gallery Singapore magazine (2020)

facts.text: Already calling herself Singaporean, she built a house on Siglap Plain, where she kept a clean and orderly studio.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Georgette Chen
Christie's, Georgette Chen, Cattleya Orchid, lot essay (lot 5638044)

facts.text: Malay artist friends hunted for a Malay name containing 'Chen'; she chose Chendana, fragrant sandalwood.

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board
Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)
Wikipedia: Georgette Chen

facts.text: She called her life of part-time teaching 'bread without butter', adding that she did not much like butter anyway.
facts.quote: I don't like butter much anyway, too fattening!
facts.speaker: Georgette Chen (letter, 6 Feb 1961)

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

facts.text: Rheumatoid arthritis, which had afflicted her father too, began in her 40s; one attack left her 'hobbling on a stick for months and months'.

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

facts.text: She cooked for friends (oyster soup, fillet mignon, 'Crepes Georgette'), gave cooking demonstrations for the YWCA in 1960 and 1961, and left a banana cake recipe.

sources.label: Michelle Tay, 'The World of Georgette Chen Archive', National Gallery Singapore magazine (2020)

facts.text: In 1962 she sat the Malay oral and written exams, cramming from 6 a.m., as nervous as the young candidates; she passed and got her diploma.
facts.quote: I felt as nervous as the young candidates who took part.
facts.speaker: Georgette Chen (letter, 1962)

sources.label: Michelle Tay, 'The World of Georgette Chen Archive', National Gallery Singapore magazine (2020)

facts.text: To her former student Patricia Kennison she joked that she sometimes felt 'quite PATRAQUE', like an old machine that runs badly.

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

facts.text: She summed up her life to Eugene's cousin Dorothy Lee and promised her pictures to Singapore and Malaysia.
facts.quote: I have continued to be myself seeking neither fame nor riches.
facts.speaker: Georgette Chen (letter to Dorothy Lee, 17 May 1967)

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

facts.text: Students knew her as an excellent but strict teacher, elegant and methodical; Liu Kang said she taught not just technique but the ethics of making art.

sources.label: Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)

facts.text: A serious fall in 1981 put her in hospital; she needed care for the rest of her life.

sources.label: Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

facts.text: She became the first woman visual artist to receive the Cultural Medallion; too ill to attend, her former student Ng Eng Teng collected it for her.

sources.label: Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'
Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)
Wikipedia: Georgette Chen

facts.text: In oral-history interviews with Constance Sheares she said an artist must be prepared to starve, but loves the work too much to stop.
facts.quote: An artist, I tell you, has to be prepared to starve.
facts.speaker: Georgette Chen (interview with Constance Sheares, 1988-89)

sources.label: Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)

facts.text: She died on 15 March 1993 at Mount Alvernia Hospital from complications of rheumatoid arthritis.

sources.label: Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)
Wikipedia: Georgette Chen

facts.text: Her executor found 53 paintings stowed in two rooms of her Siglap Plain house and gave them to the Singapore Art Museum; the house sold for S$2.8 million to fund an arts scholarship.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Georgette Chen
Esplanade Offstage, TributeSG: 'Georgette Chen Liying' (12 Oct 2016, updated 27 Nov 2025)
Culturepaedia (Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre), 'Pioneer artist: Georgette Chen'

facts.text: She left carbon copies of some 1,000 letters, 27 diaries and her beloved Hermes Baby typewriter, now in the National Gallery archive.

sources.label: Michelle Tay, 'The World of Georgette Chen Archive', National Gallery Singapore magazine (2020)
Sara Siew, 'Georgette Chen: The Artist Speaks', BiblioAsia vol. 15 issue 2 (Jul-Sep 2019), National Library Board

conflicts.detail: Her marriage certificate says October 1906, Zhejiang (BiblioAsia, Esplanade). Her Singapore passports say 17 October 1907, China; her teacher registration form and a 1953 exhibition note say Paris; Christie's says 'born in Paris in 1907'; Wikipedia gives 23 October 1906. The National Gallery curators conclude China, 1906. Using October 1906, Zhejiang.
